title: Fault-tolerant cost of shallow QAOA on near-symmetric optimization problems
authors: Jernej Rudi Finžgar, Martin Leib, Elisabeth Wybo
abstract: Montanaro and Zhou proved that depth-one Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) finds the planted solution of certain near-symmetric constraint satisfaction problems with probability $Ω(1)$, and observed exponential runtimes for general-purpose classical solvers on explicit realizations, providing strong evidence of an empirical exponential speedup of low-depth QAOA. We ask what such a circuit costs fault-tolerantly. Although the cost Hamiltonian carries $Θ(n^\ell)$ clauses, the rotation angle at which QAOA succeeds shrinks as $n^{1-\ell}$, and we show that small-angle Clifford$+T$ rotation synthesis reduces the non-Clifford cost per circuit to $\widetilde O(n^2)$ for every clause locality $\ell$. Compiling the circuit, however, requires the explicit clause list. We find that the mechanism underlying constant QAOA success fixes the degree-one Fourier coefficients of the cost, whose signs reveal the planted solution. However, this leakage need not reveal the solution: we design families in which the quadratic non-Clifford scaling and hard exact optimization coexist.
summary: This work analyzes the fault-tolerant resource cost of running shallow QAOA circuits on structured optimization problems. By employing small-angle rotation synthesis, the required non-Clifford gate cost is significantly reduced to $eO(n^2)$. This analysis confirms the exponential quantum speedup while providing critical resource estimates necessary for hardware implementation.
main_problem: The paper determines the fault-tolerant resource cost required to execute shallow Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) circuits for solving near-symmetric optimization problems.
main_result: Small-angle synthesis reduces the non-Clifford gate cost per circuit to $eO(n^2)$, enabling the study of larger problems while maintaining an exponential speedup over classical solvers.
method: The analysis uses small-angle Clifford+T rotation synthesis and compares resource scaling across different circuit decomposition methods (quasi-probability vs. probability mixture).
model_or_system: The model is fault-tolerant quantum computation implemented on a surface-code-based architecture, using QAOA circuits to solve constraint satisfaction problems.
key_observables: Success Probability ($\Omega(1)$), Non-Clifford Cost ($eO(n^2)$), Degree-one Fourier coefficients ($h_i$).
important_parameters: Locality ($\ell$), Sparsification fraction ($f$), Phase-matched angle ($\gamma = \Theta(n^{1-\ell})$), Time limit (one-hour cap).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a surface-code-based fault-tolerant architecture and relies on the small-angle approximation holding true.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the cost reduction from the value-oracle model to the explicit clause list, showing the $eO(n^2)$ cost. Figure 2 compares the scaling of the non-Clifford cost for different QAOA depths and synthesis conventions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the empirical speedup of low-depth QAOA, derives the small-angle scaling required for success, calculates the resulting fault-tolerant gate cost using advanced synthesis techniques, and finally discusses resource limitations imposed by hardware constraints.
why_interesting: It provides concrete, resource-aware estimates for running quantum algorithms on near-term, noisy hardware, which is crucial for designing feasible quantum simulations or quantum advantage demonstrations.
